Sylvia — thanks for flagging this, great catch.

Quick summary from our side: US DST starts 2 Apr 2026, while many EU zones change a week earlier (or later depending on locale). That can cause the recurring invite to show a different ET for the single week that crosses the change.

Options we can do immediately:
1) Re-issue the series with timezone locked to Europe/Paris (that keeps EU wall-clock constant; ET will display a different local hour during the DST transition).
2) Create an exception for Apr 2 only and send a single-date invite for US attendees at a time that keeps the event at the same relative overlap (e.g., 04:00 ET on Apr 2 becomes 05:00 ET after the US shift).
3) Move the series to a slightly later UTC time so both regions have the same wall-clock on all occurrences (we can propose 11:00 CET / 05:00 ET).

Marissa and Grace — can we fast-follow on (1) vs (2)? If procurement wants a consistent EU-time invite, (1) is easiest. If the US SREs need the same ET across the board, (2) with an exception is safer.

I'll hold off making changes until I get the green light — can Sylvia confirm preferred approach?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Proposed compromise: lock series to Europe/Paris, and we create a one-off US-facing add-on invite on Apr 2 that repeats only once (so US engineers see the correct local time in their calendar for the DST week).

I'll draft the additional single-date invite and include a short note in the event description explaining the DST exception.
